citations.name: requirements.sdk.graph.criteria.deterministic_procedures
citations.commentary:
A criterion can also compute its answer with deterministic Rust code.
Its `ValidationContext` exposes the [inspection operations](validation-context.md)
used by the agent's graph tools.
[Searches and outlines](validation-context.md#find-a-node-then-read-its-contents)
help locate code to inspect; tracked reads and edge selections record input
identities and fingerprints, so changes to those inputs can invalidate the
resulting evidence.

rationale:
The passage is explanatory prose that uses {cite}, and its claims agree with the cited declarations.

- `requirements.sdk.graph.criteria.deterministic_procedures` says a criterion can compute its answer directly from tracked inputs without a configured agent. That matches the first sentence about deterministic Rust code.
- `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.shared_context` says direct reads and reads served by the agent tools record inputs in the same `ValidationContext`. That supports the claim that the context exposes the operations the agent's tools use, and that reads are tracked.
- `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.behavior` and `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.outline_source.behavior` describe search and outline results that return node references. That is consistent with searches and outlines helping to locate code to inspect.
- `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.inputs` says evidence keeps the observed dependencies, which are node handles with domain-defined edge labels. That supports the claim that reads and edge selections record input identities.
- `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records` says recorded dependencies are compared by fingerprint, and a mismatch makes the check return `Ok(false)`. That supports the claim that changed inputs can invalidate the evidence.

I found no contradicted or unsupported claims. The citation roles are correct, because prose uses {cite}. No citation is redundant.

text: :::{req} deterministic_procedures
`Criterion::execute` can compute an answer without a configured model provider.
A criterion can compute its answer directly using tracked inputs; deterministic
execution needs no configured agent.
:::{req} shared_context
During one call to `verify`, direct reads by the criterion and
reads served by the SDK's agent tools record inputs in the same
`ValidationContext`. For example, if criterion code reads a test and the agent
then reads its helper, both node fingerprints accompany the returned answer.
A subsequent verification starts with an empty dependency list.
:::{req} search_text.behavior

The harness groups matching occurrences under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits` and renders each excerpt under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.windows`. Each entry's `node` is a reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. `complete` reports whether the search exhausted its scope.
:::{req} outline_source.behavior
The outline uses the file snapshot retained by the domain’s cache. Each item includes its kind and a reference the agent can pass to `read_node`. Follow `next` to see more items.
:::{req} inputs
Keeps a typed output with its source, criterion, version, and observed dependencies. `output` borrows the answer and `into_output` consumes the wrapper.
`verify` constructs this value from the criterion's completed answer and
execution trace. `load_evidence` reconstructs it from the selected saved record.
Its dependencies use `NodeId<D>` handles from the current cache and domain-defined edge labels.
```rust,ignore
pub struct Fingerprinted<D: Domain, O> { /* private fields */ }
impl<D: Domain, O> Fingerprinted<D, O> {
pub fn source_node_id(&self) -> &NodeId<D>;
pub fn criterion_path(&self) -> &CriterionPath;
pub fn version(&self) -> Option<&CriterionVersion>;
pub fn dependencies(&self) -> &[Dependency<NodeId<D>, D::EdgeLabel>];
pub fn output(&self) -> &O;
pub fn into_output(self) -> O;
:::{req} checking_records
The method is declared under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.check_inputs`.
The method resolves the recorded dependencies through graph operations and
fingerprinting, comparing each with its saved observation. A fingerprint
mismatch returns `Ok(false)` and permits an early return; it need not resolve
later dependencies. An encountered dependency-resolution failure returns an
error.
The method observes the current state that the caller intends to inspect.
Freshness checking has a separate observation scope from criterion execution.
Checked observations enter the new trace when execution explicitly reads
or delivers them.
A checked snapshot can be reused if it still represents the current state.
